news.title: Vietnam earn historic U17 World Cup point, drawing praise from FIFA and fans
news.lede: New Zealand took the lead in the 19th minute when Jack Clegg converted a low cross from Matias Nunez, leaving Vietnam trailing 1-0 at halftime. Vietnam responded in the 49th minute through Chu Ngoc Nguyen Luc, whose dangerous free kick beat goalkeeper Joseph Chalari at the near post. However, John Woldegiorgis quickly restored New Zealand's advantage with a close-range header. Nguyen Luc continued to impress, delivering an exquisite pass for Le Trong Dai Nhan to equalize in the 58th minute.

news.title: Duo’s return excites Kerr as final World Cup auditions get underway
news.lede: Sam Kerr is eager to take on the biggest stage in women’s football for the fifth time in her career next year, but she insists there is still work to do before then. Kerr was in disbelief as she spoke to reporters on Tuesday about the looming World Cup in Brazil in July with the Matildas, admitting she is still coming to terms with the idea the 2023 World Cup being more than three years ago. Sam Kerr is back in Australia ahead of Australia’s games against Colombia. The team reached new heights on and off the field at that home tournament, taking the nation on a rollercoaster journey to finish fourth overall.

news.title: Another chance at history: PNG Bilums chase FIFA World Cup dream - ABC Pacific
news.lede: For a few moments after the final whistle in Auckland, Papua New Guinea forward Yvonne Gabong didn't know what to feel. The PNG Bilums had just lost 1-0 to New Zealand in the final of the Oceania qualifiers for the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup, finishing one goal short of a place in football's biggest tournament. "We felt like we had won, but somehow we hadn't," Gabong said. The disappointment was immense, but so too was the achievement.

news.title: Fifa to have final say over dynamic pricing for 2035 Women's World Cup in UK, FA admits
news.lede: Enjoy your favourite LBC shows with ad-free Catch Up, weekly competition entries and an exclusive newsletter. Fifa will decide whether dynamic ticket pricing is used for the 2035 Women's World Cup in the UK, a Football Association official has said. Sue Day, the FA's director of women's football, said the four host nations hoped to have a "strong influence" over ticket sales and wanted the tournament to be accessible. England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales were confirmed as hosts of the 48-team tournament at an extraordinary Fifa Congress on November 23.

news.title: World Cup 2035: Belfast to welcome football’s biggest stars as calls grow for Windsor Park investment
news.lede: Northern Ireland is set to host matches at the 2035 FIFA Women’s World Cup after the United Kingdom’s joint bid received final approval from world football’s governing body, bringing one of the sport’s biggest international tournaments to Belfast. The National Football Stadium at Windsor Park is included in plans for the competition, with proposals to increase its capacity from 18,000 to 23,750 as preparations turn towards meeting FIFA’s hosting requirements. The tournament will be staged across England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, featuring 48 national teams and 104 matches. It will be the first time Northern Ireland has hosted fixtures at a FIFA Women’s World Cup.
